clue.text: US tip: party is at hotel over the weekend

indicators.note: the party word sits over, that is covers and surrounds, the end of the week

parts.note: a bash is a lively party
the end of the word week is its last letter K
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American explains a tipping rule involving a party at a hotel on a weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' points to the American spelling of the word more often written baksheesh; the end of the word 'week' is K.
explanation.definitionFit: Baksheesh, in this variant spelling listed by American dictionaries, is a gratuity or small bribe in the Middle East.

clue.text: 10 and 21's field, where being concise is silly, when no good comes from it

indicators.note: silly signals the phrase's letters are scrambled

explanation.walkthrough: BEING CONCISE has the answer's letters plus N and G: 'when no good comes from it' takes NG out.
explanation.definitionFit: Watson and Crick, numbered 10 and 21, worked in molecular biology, a life-sciences discipline.

explanation.definitionFit: The Erne is a river in Ireland, flowing through Fermanagh, so a watercourse with banks.

explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, making a great fuss of them.
